# RustyNES v2.7.6 — "Recount"

A measurement release between the two halves of the audit line that [ADR 0041](https://github.com/doublegate/RustyNES/blob/main/docs/adr/0041-hardware-release-is-v3.0.0.md) put before the SuperStation One core (**v3.0.0**). v2.7.5 closed the core audit's performance proposals, but six of them were measured only together. This release measures each one alone. All six are zero, and one of them turned out to be better written as an assertion than as code.

It also ships the libretro buildbot work contributed by @WizzardSK in #554: the macOS RetroArch cores build again, and 32-bit Windows, 32-bit Linux and webOS targets are new.

**No emulation behaviour changes.** The one code change is a debug assertion, compiled out of release builds, so every release binary is byte-identical in behaviour to v2.7.5. **The MiSTer sibling does not change, and no new bitstream is cut.** No hardware has run any bitstream; the board session is v2.9.2.

## Six proposals, measured one at a time

v2.7.5 applied seven of the core audit's hot-path proposals in one tree, deleting the work outright, and measured the result: a ceiling on what the set could win. It came back zero. But a combined bound is a bound on the sum. One proposal's real gain could be cancelled by another's code-layout loss, which is the same size as the gains being looked for, and a benchmark can fail to reach the code at all. The second is not hypothetical: the audio-buffer change (IMP-07) sat inside that combined zero until review showed the benchmarks never drain audio, and measured where it acts it was adopted.

Only one of the seven, the branchless status-flag rewrite, had been measured alone. The other six are measured alone here:

| Proposal | What the probe deleted |
| --- | --- |
| §3.1 A | the CPU clock-divider lookup, hard-coded to NTSC |
| §3.1 B | the DMA master-clock drain check at the end of every CPU cycle |
| §3.1 C | the NMI edge sample in every PPU catch-up loop |
| IMP-06 | four redundant stores in the fast render path |
| §3.5b | the pulse channels' sweep-mute check |
| §3.6 | the unmapped-read check on every cartridge read |

Each ran through `scripts/perf/ab_check.sh` twice, independently, on the four shipped frame workloads, and each run re-benches the reference against itself afterwards as an order-bias control. Each probe's output was also hashed over 180 frames of picture and audio on both benchmark ROMs and both dot paths.

**All six are zero, and all six are byte-identical to the unprobed build.** No workload is faster than its own control in both runs. The cells that stand out are slower, and do not repeat in the other run: code layout and background load, which is what the two-run rule exists to catch. The full table is in `docs/performance.md` §v2.7.6.

## What the one-at-a-time look found

**Three of the four fast-path stores wrote a value the code already guarantees.** The fast render path is entered only when the PPU's rendering history is stably enabled, and it then wrote `true` into three history fields that the entry check had just required to be `true`. Their comment said they were kept "to stay byte-identical", but writing a value a field already holds cannot change anything. They are now a `debug_assert!` of the guarantee: nothing in a release build, and a check in every debug and test build that fails if a future change to the entry check stops providing it. The fourth store is not covered by the entry check and stays.

That assertion needed its own test, and finding that out is the useful result. Weakening the entry check, first by one term and then by all of the history terms, left the fast-path differential test green both times: another term alone keeps every such dot in the test corpus off the fast path, so no ROM reaches a state that breaks the guarantee. A unit test now enters the fast path with a lagging history and requires the assertion to fire; restoring the old stores turns it red.

**Two of the deletions remove dead work.** The NMI edge sample (§3.1 C) fills a latch whose only reader is `poll_nmi`, one of the bus methods deprecated in v2.7.5 with no caller since v2.0.0; the CPU has detected the NMI edge itself since then. The DMA drain check (§3.1 B) guards an accumulator that only a unit-test path feeds. Removing them properly means removing those deprecated methods too, and that is the API decision ADR 0041 holds for v2.9.0, so they are recorded and left in place.

## Libretro buildbot (contributed by @WizzardSK, #554)

- **The macOS RetroArch cores build again.** Both macOS buildbot jobs had failed in every pipeline: libretro's macOS templates set `SDKROOT` in a `before_script` that each job's own `before_script` replaced, so the bindings were generated against Linux headers. Both jobs now set it themselves. The first pipeline after the merge built all fifteen jobs green.
- **New buildbot targets: 32-bit Windows, 32-bit Linux, and webOS** (armv7a and aarch64). The first three publish to live download trees, so those cores reach RetroArch's Online Updater. webOS aarch64 is a build target only for now: the buildbot has no `webos/aarch64` download tree yet.
- The Linux aarch64 job now builds from libretro's own aarch64 template, and the GitHub `libretro-cross` gate rehearses the new 32-bit triples on every pull request.

The v2.7.5 release also gained the libretro cores from that first green pipeline, for the platforms where a core can be installed from a downloaded file.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| AccuracyCoin (RAM decoder) | 144 / 144 |
| nestest | pass |
| `--features test-roms` workspace suite | 154 suites, 2,722 passed, 0 failed |
| Fast-path differential test, debug build (assertion live) | 5 / 5 |
| Mutation | restoring the old stores turns `fast_render_path_asserts_its_rendering_history` red |
| fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `no_std` build, release-anchor audits | clean |
| Performance | two `ab_check.sh` runs per proposal, 25 s per sample set, four shipped workloads, each read against its own A/B/A control, plus a 180-frame output hash per probe |

**Next:** v2.8.0 resumes the libretro audit: panic containment in the RetroArch core, the standard game-loading path, memory-map teardown, save-state sizing for expansion devices, and the internal data bus in save states.
